body: This is a partly a duplicate issue of [Issue #478 - 1.1.5 broke relative paths](https://github.com/cloudhead/less.js/issues/478)

issue.title: fixed bug in less.js where relative `url()`s were being resvolved based ...
issue.body:
...on the path of the containing .less file, instead of the original (topmost) .less file.

This brings the behavior of less.js in line with lessc.

Fixes #471 & #465 and probably a few others.

body: @cloudhead this is still broken in LESS 1.2.2. Importing CSS is a very common use case. Mind taking a look at the pull request by @maranomynet ?

issue.title: url() bug

body: seems like although that bug is fixed, this one isn't? let me know if its actually closed.

the actual original bug is fixed.

The only remaining bug is that node lessc is relative to the base less file and browser is relative to the current less file.

This is picked up in #483

Hi agatronic: Based on your last comment, which do you see as the correct fix?  Should imported files be interpreted as relative to the base less file or the current less file?  My take is it should be relative to the current less file (i.e. the file that defines the url(...)), not the file that imports it, however the pull request for #483 takes the opposite interpretation.

repository.name: less4j
repository.description: Less language is an extension of css and less4j compiles it into regular css. Less adds several dynamic features into css: variables, expressions, nested rules, and so on. Less was designed to be compatible with css and any correct css file is also correct less file.
